app.title: Linstruct — your AI instruction files, as each agent reads them
headline.no_host: No AI host found on this machine — the hosts below show what they would read.
headline.clear: Your instruction files, as {hosts} read them: nothing to act on, nothing to review.
headline.review: Your instruction files, as {hosts} read them: nothing to act on now, {review} to review.
headline.act: Your instruction files, as {hosts} read them: {act} to act on now, {review} to review.
kpi.findings.sub: {act} act now · {review} review · {know} good to know · {info} info
kind.cut: Content you wrote is not read: the host cuts or skips it, and nothing tells you.
kind.secret: A credential sits in a file that is sent with every request.
kind.over-limit: The file is past a limit the host documents; what the host does then is not documented.
kind.ignored: The host never reads this file; the instructions in it have no effect there.
kind.dead-import: A reference that brings nothing in: the target is missing, too deep, or the host does not expand references.
kind.frontmatter: The rule does not apply the way its header says.
kind.shadowed: The host reads this kind of file, but another file takes its place here.
kind.over-length: Longer than the host recommends; every line costs context on every request and dilutes the rest.
kind.duplicate: The same text is loaded twice by this host and paid twice.
kind.comments: HTML comments are sent to the model by this host.
kind.legacy: An older name the host still reads, replaced by a newer one.
kind.unreadable: The file could not be read.

about.title: Linstruct
about.body: For each AI host on this machine and each project you work in, Linstruct rebuilds the stack of instruction files the host would load — in its order, references expanded, budget simulated — and says what it would cut, ignore or shadow. It reads; it never writes.
